desc: Parse input: N and the N×N character grid; build adjacency structures: out_edges[v] as dict letter → list of destinations, and in_edges[v] as dict letter → list of sources.
Initialize dist as N×N array filled with -1; set dist[i][i] = 0 and dist[i][j] = 1 for every edge i→j; enqueue all such states in a deque (multi-source BFS).

BFS transition: for state (u, v) with distance d, for each letter present in both in_edges[u] and out_edges[v], for each predecessor x of u and successor y of v with that letter, if dist[x][y] unset, set to d+2 and enqueue.
Verify correctness reasoning: prove BFS layers correspond to palindrome lengths (even lengths via diagonal seeds, odd via edge seeds) and that first visit yields the minimum.

Analyze complexity: states ≤ N² = 10⁴; each transition expansion bounded by sum over letters of indeg·outdeg products; worst case dense graph ~N⁴ = 10⁸ — resolved via bitmask-row dedup reducing work to ~N·E ≈ 10⁶ big-int ops.
Implement solve() reading N and grid, building per-vertex per-letter in-neighbor lists, out-neighbor bitmasks, and letter-presence bitmasks.
Initialize BFS queue with all (i,i) at distance 0, then all edge pairs (i,j) at distance 1 (skip if already set, e.g., self-loop where dist=0).
Run BFS: for each state, iterate common letters; for each predecessor x compute new target bitmask = out_mask & ~vis[x]; for each set bit y set dist, mark visited, enqueue.
Sanity-check algorithm against both provided samples via manual BFS trace (e.g., (1,4)=4 via abba in sample 1; (5,3)=5 in sample 2).
